introduction_markdown: Duration: Three Hours. Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION C: PRESCRIBED TEXTS (20 marks)**

Answer ONE question only.

questions.enonce_markdown: **4.** With reference to any three prescribed texts, show how writers use humour to reveal character.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method answer (corrigé de méthode : the prescribed texts are not available, so no detail of any work is given)**

**Plan of a full-mark essay (about 450 to 500 words, three texts)**

1. Introduction: define humour (comic situation, irony, exaggeration, wit) and name the three texts.
2. Paragraph for each text: a comic episode or remark, and the character it reveals.
3. State what the humour reveals (vanity, ignorance, greed, hypocrisy, wisdom) and the technique (irony, exaggeration, comic speech, contrast, understatement).
4. Conclusion: humour lets the writer criticise gently, and makes the characters memorable.

**Model paragraph frame (to be filled with the candidate's own text knowledge)**

*In [title] by [author], [character/episode] shows [point of the question]. For example, [precise episode or quotation]. The writer achieves this through [technique], which makes the reader [feel / judge]. This is similar to / different from [link with the next text].*

**Marking criteria (20 marks)**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Relevance to the question | The essay answers exactly what is asked (humour, character, technique) for the right number of texts and characters |
| Knowledge of the texts | Accurate, specific examples from each text, not vague summary |
| Analysis | Explains the writer's technique and effect, not only what happens |
| Organisation and expression | A clear introduction, one paragraph for each text, a conclusion, correct and fluent English |

**Common mistakes**

1. Retelling the plot without answering the question, or using fewer texts than the question requires.
2. Giving examples from the wrong texts, or inventing details of a work that the candidate has not studied.
